title: First observation of microscopic life
summary: Using a hand-ground single-lens microscope, Leeuwenhoek observed and described what he called animalcules in pond water, the first documented sighting of microorganisms.

title: Disproof of spontaneous generation
summary: Pasteur's swan-neck flask experiments showed that sterilized broth stayed free of microbial growth unless exposed to airborne particles, refuting spontaneous generation.

title: Antiseptic hand-washing reduces childbed fever
summary: Semmelweis showed that hand disinfection with chlorinated lime sharply cut maternal mortality, though germ theory did not yet exist to explain why.

title: Formulation of Koch's postulates
summary: Koch articulated a set of criteria for establishing a causal link between a microorganism and a disease, becoming the methodological foundation of medical microbiology.

title: Development of the Gram stain
summary: Gram's differential staining method distinguished bacteria by cell-wall structure and remains a first-line diagnostic tool.

title: First rabies vaccination in a human
summary: Pasteur administered his experimental rabies vaccine to a boy bitten by a rabid dog, one of the earliest successful uses of a lab-developed vaccine in humans.

title: Discovery of viruses as filterable agents
summary: Ivanovsky showed the tobacco mosaic agent passed through bacteria-trapping filters; Beijerinck's 1898 follow-up work named it a contagium vivum fluidum, founding virology.

title: Discovery of bacteriophages
summary: D'Herelle identified viruses capable of infecting and destroying bacteria, coining the term bacteriophage; Frederick Twort had observed a similar phenomenon independently in 1915.

title: Discovery of penicillin
summary: Fleming noticed that Penicillium mold contamination on a culture plate killed nearby Staphylococcus colonies, launching the antibiotic era.

title: Discovery of bacterial transformation
summary: Griffith showed that harmless pneumococci could acquire virulence traits from heat-killed virulent bacteria, hinting at a transferable genetic substance.

title: DNA identified as the genetic material
people: Oswald Avery; Colin MacLeod; Maclyn McCarty
summary: Building on Griffith's transformation experiment, this team showed DNA, not protein, carried pneumococcal genetic information.

title: Discovery of bacterial conjugation
summary: Demonstrated that bacteria could exchange genetic material through direct cell-to-cell contact, founding the field of bacterial genetics.

title: Isolation of streptomycin
summary: Isolated from Streptomyces griseus, streptomycin became the first antibiotic effective against tuberculosis.

title: Discovery of transduction
summary: Showed that bacteriophages could transfer bacterial genes between cells, a third mechanism of horizontal gene transfer alongside conjugation and transformation.

title: Hershey-Chase experiment confirms DNA as genetic material
summary: Using radioactively labeled bacteriophages, the experiment showed that DNA, not protein, is injected into bacteria to direct viral replication.

title: Elucidation of the DNA double helix
people: James Watson; Francis Crick; Rosalind Franklin; Maurice Wilkins
summary: Watson and Crick's model, built on Franklin's X-ray diffraction data, revealed DNA's double-helix structure, transforming microbial genetics.

title: Isolation of HIV
summary: Isolated a retrovirus from a lymph node biopsy that was later confirmed as the cause of AIDS.

title: Invention of the polymerase chain reaction
summary: Devised a method to exponentially amplify specific DNA sequences in vitro, becoming a foundational tool across microbiology and diagnostics.

title: Archaea recognized as a distinct domain of life
summary: Comparative analysis of 16S ribosomal RNA sequences revealed that archaea are as distinct from bacteria as both are from eukaryotes.

title: Discovery of deep-sea hydrothermal vent ecosystems
summary: Found dense communities of life sustained by chemosynthetic bacteria rather than sunlight, expanding the known limits of habitable environments.

title: Helicobacter pylori linked to stomach ulcers
summary: Marshall drank a culture of the bacterium to demonstrate it caused gastritis, overturning decades of belief that ulcers were caused by stress and acid alone.

title: First bacterial genome fully sequenced
summary: The genome of Haemophilus influenzae was the first complete genome sequence of any free-living organism.

title: First archaeal genome fully sequenced
people: Carol Bult, Craig Venter and colleagues
summary: Sequencing of Methanocaldococcus jannaschii's genome confirmed archaea's deep genetic distinctiveness from bacteria.

title: Human Microbiome Project launched
summary: A large-scale initiative to catalogue the microbial communities living in and on the human body, reshaping understanding of health and disease.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 developed as a gene-editing tool
summary: Adapted a bacterial immune defense mechanism into a programmable gene-editing tool, earning the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

title: Identification and sequencing of SARS-CoV-2
people: Chinese CDC and collaborating research teams
summary: The virus behind a cluster of pneumonia cases was identified and its genome published within weeks, enabling rapid global diagnostic and vaccine development.

title: Discovery of restriction enzymes
people: Hamilton Smith; Daniel Nathans; Werner Arber
summary: Identification of bacterial enzymes that cut DNA at specific sequences enabled recombinant DNA technology; shared the 1978 Nobel Prize.

title: First recombinant DNA organism
summary: Combined DNA from different species into a functioning bacterial genome, founding modern genetic engineering.

title: Genetically engineered bacteria produce human insulin
summary: Escherichia coli was engineered to produce synthetic human insulin, the first genetically engineered drug, approved for use in 1982.

title: Discovery of CRISPR sequences in bacteria
summary: Mojica identified repeated DNA sequences in archaea and bacteria that were later understood to form an adaptive immune system against viruses.

title: CRISPR gene-drive system reverses antibiotic resistance in bacteria
people: Ethan Bier; Justin Meyer and colleagues, UC San Diego
summary: The pPro-MobV system spreads a CRISPR-based genetic cassette through bacterial populations, actively deleting antibiotic-resistance genes rather than just killing resistant cells, including within biofilms.
